title: Fix concurrent benchmark materialization race
description:
Concurrent corpus preparation exposes a materializer race. When one process creates tests/benchmark/.cache/repos/<key>@<commit> and is still cloning or checking out, a second pnpm run benchmark:materialize <key> sees the directory, immediately runs git rev-parse HEAD, and exits 128 because HEAD is not yet resolvable. It neither waits nor recovers, despite the cache eventually becoming valid.

Reproduced during parallel easy-school packet preparation in the separate corpus-curation worktree. The current existing-directory validation assumes a completed Git checkout; it must safely handle a partially created target.

Acceptance criteria:
- Concurrent invocations for the same repo key do not fail or corrupt the cache.
- Use a per-key lock or materialize into a temporary sibling directory and atomically rename only after complete validation.
- An empty, partial, or non-Git target is treated as incomplete and recovered or reported with an actionable non-crashing result.
- Add a deterministic test covering the partial-target or concurrent path.
- Keep materialization opt-in and outside normal CI.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Additional independent reproduction while materializing Keycloak: clone target was created, but after the materialize command returned it still had no resolvable HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` exits 128). This confirms partial-target recovery is required in addition to concurrency protection.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Third independent reproduction during Medusa materialization: target clone directory exists but `git rev-parse HEAD` exits 128 after the materializer invocation. This is consistent with the partial-target recovery defect, not a corpus failure.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Fixed on develop via PR #3 (materialize orchestrator: per-key lock, ownership token, used-existing follower, stale/abandoned recovery). Duplicate of the DATAP-b80122 family. Closing.
